correctness.rationale: Only equilateral boundary triples maximize area. In two orientation charts the deficit has uniform normal form c sum radial deficits plus positive-definite angular quadratic B, with c=sqrt(3)/2 and sqrt(det B)=3/8. The exact independent radial/angle Jacobian, boundary regular variation, dominated convergence, 3-simplex beta integral, and circular angular phase establish both coefficient and full Dirichlet limit. Reproducible finite importance-sampling checks agree within numerical uncertainty; limits are proven analytically.

value.rationale: The three-point disk maximum-area event is a natural stochastic-geometric observable. Its exact rare-event exponent depends on radial boundary mass, while its amplitude carries a threefold sampling correlation; the entire conditional shape has a universal Dirichlet law. This distinguishes interior sampling from known circle-boundary extremes and supplies a motivated multiscale conditional invariant beyond a scalar tail coefficient.
